questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Destination: Toronto, Canada.
The cross-cultural atmosphere that fills everyday life in Toronto is one of the main reasons why I chose an exchange stay at University of Toronto (UofT) really appealing. In addition, UofT has the reputation of being among the best in the world and has a highly recognized faculty of economics, which is essential for me studying economics.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had an amazing experience. The only thing was that the first month in Toronto was in lockdown, and the University was online for the first two months.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was ok despite the fact that I arrived in a lockdown. The online system is quite similar to the one at University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I only had contact with the exchange office if I had questions, they never contacted me. However, when you contacted the exchange office they were always sweet and helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: We had one online orientation, but due to Covid we did not have any get together events through UofT. It would have been nice with more social gatherings for exchange students through the University.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy because I knew a girl who had been in Toronto on exchange before and she recommended the student residence I ended up staying in. I would definitely recommend other students traveling to Toronto to live in a student residence or a co-up.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I did not know any students living on campus, so I would definitely recommend staying off campus. I know that there are a lot of scams regarding housing in Toronto, but I did not hear about from any I knew.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to sent a document for each course you wanted to be listed in. As an exchange student you are not able to click through the system the same way as normal registered students. So, it was a lot of work! Also with getting new pre-approvals from University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The office. They were busy, but quick and very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got most of the courses I wanted to.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It takes a lot of work if you are a graduate student (in Denmark) applying for undergraduate courses at UofT, because getting pre-approvals from UCPH and also be approved to take the course at UofT can be very complicated. However, it all works out, and the office is very helpful. Just be patient.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 300 and 400 level courses, which is considered 3rd and 4th year courses. The level was definitely ok.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar, lectures each week and in some courses additional TA-hours. However, one of the big differences is that you are judged by hand-ins, midterms and final exams. So, your grade is depended on work during the entire semester and not only exam. I really liked this structure.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Market Design (400-level)
- Health Economics (300-level)
- Markets, Competetion, and Strategy (300-level)
- Energy and Environment, Economics, Politics, and Sustainability (400-level)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was a big fan of 'Market Design' and 'Energy and Environment, Economics, Politics, and Sustainability'. Both of these courses had one big final paper. For the market design course I had to develop a mechanism, that solved a market problem, and for the Energy-course, I had the chance to write about the current gas-crisis in Europe. This was really interesting to me. I like when I can use my knowledge in a real situation.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Groceries were much more expensive than expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries are very expensive! Canada is importing many food products, so vegetables and fruits are more expensive compared to Danish prices. However, going out to eat was not that expensive compared to making food at home. So, you have an incentive to explore the many great restaurants in Toronto :)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was limited in the beginning due to Covid, but got better and better.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I was a part of a choir and used the athletic center a lot with friends.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Especially to use the many difference athletic options that UofT offers.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out and enjoy the many good food spots in Toronto. It's affordable and very good.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Canada is not that different from Denmark as I would expect other places to be.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Make sure to be a part of the exchange WhatsApp groups, and maybe also some of the discord groups.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There are quite a lot of homeless people, and that was hard for me to accept.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The diversity in Toronto is amazing, and that is also reflected at the University.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
-> Save money before traveling and apply for scholarships, so you can explore and travel while being there - Canada is AMAZING 
-> Explore Toronto and its diversity 
-> Join WhatsApp and Discord chats. It's where (exchange) students connect.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I have learned and experienced so many things during the last 5 months. However, the most rewarding part must be the many new friends I have made through these months. I have made friends for a life time.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being apart from family and friends back home. I'm very close to my family and friends in Denmark, so being apart from them for so long definitely was a challenge. However, it was worth it, and you meet so many new interesting people, that the 5 months goes by so fast. Before you know it, you are back home again.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: You should definitely study abroad. It is an amazing opportunity and a life time experience.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
